patterns.title: RAG Chunking Strategies
patterns.problem: Retrieving whole documents floods the context window with mostly-irrelevant text and buries the passage that actually answers the question.
patterns.tradeoff: Small chunks improve retrieval precision but fragment meaning — an answer can get separated from the sentence that qualifies it. Large chunks preserve coherence but spend budget on padding around the relevant part.

patterns.title: Context Compression & Summarization
patterns.problem: Long-running conversations and large source documents exceed the context budget before the model ever gets to the current question.
patterns.tradeoff: Compression is lossy by definition — a summary written now can silently drop the one detail a later turn needs, and there's rarely a way to know which detail that'll be in advance.

patterns.title: Short-term vs. Long-term Memory
patterns.problem: Not everything worth remembering fits in one context window, and not everything currently in the window is worth carrying past this turn.
patterns.tradeoff: Splitting memory into a working window and a persisted store adds retrieval latency and a staleness risk — the long-term store becomes its own context-rot problem if nothing curates what gets written to it or when it's pulled back in.

patterns.title: Tool-Result Truncation
patterns.problem: A single tool call — a file read, an API response, a search result page — can return more tokens than the rest of the context budget combined.
patterns.tradeoff: Truncate too aggressively and the model reasons over partial data without knowing it's partial, which is often worse than an obvious error would have been.

patterns.title: Prompt / Context Caching
patterns.problem: Re-sending an unchanged system prompt, tool schema set, and reference material on every turn costs latency and money without changing what's actually available to the model.
patterns.tradeoff: Caching only pays off for a stable prefix — reorder or edit anything upstream of the cache boundary and the whole thing invalidates, which quietly pushes context layout toward rigidity just to protect the cache.

patterns.title: Structured vs. Freeform Injection
patterns.problem: When retrieved facts and tool output get pasted into context as one undifferentiated block of text, the model has no reliable way to tell which source said what — especially once there are three or four sources in the same turn.
patterns.tradeoff: Explicit structure (tags, headers, source attribution) spends tokens on markup instead of content, and over-structuring can chop up material that would have read more clearly as continuous prose.

antipatterns.title: Context Rot
antipatterns.description: Facts injected early in a long-running conversation go stale as the underlying state changes, but nothing removes or supersedes them — so the model has both the old and the new answer available, with no signal for which one is current.

antipatterns.title: Lost in the Middle
antipatterns.description: Models attend most reliably to the start and end of a long context and least reliably to the middle. A critical instruction or fact placed mid-context is technically present but functionally invisible.

antipatterns.title: Redundant Context
antipatterns.description: The same fact enters context three times — once from the system prompt, once from a retrieved document, once from conversation history — spending budget on repetition instead of coverage, and creating a contradiction the moment one copy drifts from the others.

antipatterns.title: Unbounded Context Growth in Agent Loops
antipatterns.description: Every tool call, retry, and intermediate result gets appended to the running context and nothing is ever pruned. A long enough agent loop eventually fills its own window with its own exhaust, leaving no budget for the task it was started to do.
